definition: Larceny means the legal crime of taking someone else's property unlawfully, often by stealth or trickery rather than force.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word larceny. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know larceny should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The cashier was charged with larceny after ringing up fake discounts for friends and pocketing the difference.
Pilfering is weaker than larceny — it suggests petty, small-scale sneaking, like grabbing office pens, rather than a formal criminal charge.
Robbery is stronger than larceny — it means taking property by force or threat against a person, which makes it a more violent and more serious crime.

Theft is the everyday umbrella word for stealing of any kind, at home in conversation and headlines alike. Larceny is the courtroom's version of the same idea — the precise legal name for unlawfully taking property, the word that appears on the charge sheet rather than in casual talk.

Stealing is the plainest word there is for taking what belongs to someone else — the word a child learns first. Larceny is what stealing becomes when the law picks it up: a defined crime, graded into petty and grand, charged and tried under that name.

Shoplifting is one narrow kind of stealing — sneaking goods out of a store without paying. Larceny is the broad legal category above it: the crime of unlawfully taking property by stealth or trickery, whoever the victim is — a shop, a stranger, or an employer.
